title: Factored cubic
problem: Find all real solutions of \((x^2 + 1)(x - 3) = 2(x^2 + 1)\). Check this solution — tap a step if it slips, or let it pass.
steps: Divide both sides by \(x^2 + 1\) to get \(x - 3 = 2\).
So \(x = 5\) is the only real solution.

clean_steps: Divide both sides by \(x^2 + 1\) to get \(x - 3 = 2\).

explanation: Dividing by \(x^2 + 1\) looks like a lost-root trap, except \(x^2 + 1 \ge 1\) can never hit zero for any real \(x\).
